# Data Source: stripe_treasury_transaction

A change to the balance of a Treasury financial account, made by one money movement. It lives on a connected account, so read it through a provider configuration whose `stripe_account` is that account. Look one up by its `id`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "connected_account" {
  type        = string
  description = "The connected account the object lives on."
}

provider "stripe" {
  alias          = "connected"
  stripe_account = var.connected_account
}

data "stripe_treasury_transaction" "deposit" {
  provider = stripe.connected
  id       = "trxn_1MtYCCLkdIwHu7ixgXzLiVq8"
}

output "transaction_flow_type" {
  value = data.stripe_treasury_transaction.deposit.flow_type
}
```

## Argument Reference

This data source supports the following arguments:

* `id` - (Required) The ID of the treasury transaction to read.

## Attribute Reference

This data source exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `balance_impact` - Change to a FinancialAccount's balance See [`balance_impact`](#balance_impact) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount associated with this object.
* `flow` - ID of the flow that created the Transaction.
* `flow_details` - Details of the flow that created the Transaction. See [`flow_details`](#flow_details) below.
* `flow_type` - Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Possible values: `credit_reversal`, `debit_reversal`, `inbound_transfer`, `issuing_authorization`, `other`, `outbound_payment`, `outbound_transfer`, `received_credit`, `received_debit`.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `status` - Status of the Transaction. Possible values: `open`, `posted`, `void`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`status_transitions`](#status_transitions) below.

<a id="balance_impact"></a>
### `balance_impact`

The `balance_impact` attribute supports:

* `cash` - The change made to funds the user can spend right now.
* `inbound_pending` - The change made to funds that are not spendable yet, but will become available at a later time.
* `outbound_pending` - The change made to funds in the account, but not spendable because they are being held for pending outbound flows.

<a id="flow_details"></a>
### `flow_details`

The `flow_details` attribute supports:

* `credit_reversal` - You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal. See [`flow_details.credit_reversal`](#flow_details.credit_reversal) below.
* `debit_reversal` - You can reverse some [ReceivedDebits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_debits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedDebit leads to the creation of a new object known as a DebitReversal. See [`flow_details.debit_reversal`](#flow_details.debit_reversal) below.
* `inbound_transfer` - Use [InboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) to add funds to your [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) via a PaymentMethod that is owned by you. The funds will be transferred via an ACH debit. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using InboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/into/inbound-transfers) See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer) below.
* `issuing_authorization` - When an [issued card](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing) is used to make a purchase, an Issuing `Authorization` object is created. [Authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations) must be approved for the purchase to be completed successfully. Related guide: [Issued card authorizations](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/purchases/authorizations) See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization) below.
* `outbound_payment` - Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers). Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundPayment objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) See [`flow_details.outbound_payment`](#flow_details.outbound_payment) below.
* `outbound_transfer` - Use [OutboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account. Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer) below.
* `received_credit` - ReceivedCredits represent funds sent to a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) (for example, via ACH or wire). These money movements are not initiated from the FinancialAccount. See [`flow_details.received_credit`](#flow_details.received_credit) below.
* `received_debit` - ReceivedDebits represent funds pulled from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). These are not initiated from the FinancialAccount. See [`flow_details.received_debit`](#flow_details.received_debit) below.
* `type` - Type of the flow that created the Transaction. Set to the same value as `flow_type`. Possible values: `credit_reversal`, `debit_reversal`, `inbound_transfer`, `issuing_authorization`, `other`, `outbound_payment`, `outbound_transfer`, `received_credit`, `received_debit`.

<a id="flow_details.credit_reversal"></a>
### `flow_details.credit_reversal`

The `flow_details.credit_reversal` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount to reverse funds from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `network` - The rails used to reverse the funds. Possible values: `ach`, `stripe`.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.credit_reversal`.
* `received_credit` - The ReceivedCredit being reversed.
* `status` - Status of the CreditReversal Possible values: `canceled`, `posted`, `processing`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions`](#flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions"></a>
### `flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions`

The `flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when the CreditReversal changed status to `posted`

* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.debit_reversal`.

<a id="flow_details.inbound_transfer"></a>
### `flow_details.inbound_transfer`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the InboundTransfer is able to be canceled.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `failure_details` - Details about this InboundTransfer's failure. Will be set when `status=failed` or `returned=true`. See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer.failure_details`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer.failure_details) below.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that received the funds.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `linked_flows` - See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer.linked_flows`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer.linked_flows) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.inbound_transfer`.
* `origin_payment_method` - The origin payment method to be debited for an InboundTransfer.
* `origin_payment_method_details` - Details about the PaymentMethod for an InboundTransfer. See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details) below.
* `returned` - Returns `true` if the funds for an InboundTransfer were returned after the InboundTransfer went to the `succeeded` state.
* `statement_descriptor` - Statement descriptor shown when funds are debited from the source. Not all payment networks support `statement_descriptor`.
* `status` - Status of the InboundTransfer: `processing`, `succeeded`, `failed`, and `canceled`. An InboundTransfer is `processing` if it is created and pending. The status changes to `succeeded` once the funds have been "confirmed" and a `transaction` is created and posted. The status changes to `failed` if the transfer fails. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `processing`, `succeeded`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer.status_transitions`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer.status_transitions) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.inbound_transfer.failure_details"></a>
### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.failure_details`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer.failure_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the failure. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `debit_not_authorized`, `incorrect_account_holder_address`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `incorrect_account_holder_tax_id`, `insufficient_funds`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.

<a id="flow_details.inbound_transfer.linked_flows"></a>
### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.linked_flows`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer.linked_flows` attribute supports:

### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the InboundTransfer. Possible values: `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.billing_details`

<a id="flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).

* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.

<a id="flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.inbound_transfer.origin_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The total amount that was authorized or rejected. This amount is in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal). `amount` should be the same as `merchant_amount`, unless `currency` and `merchant_currency` are different.
* `amount_details` - Detailed breakdown of amount components. These amounts are denominated in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.amount_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.amount_details) below.
* `approved` - Whether the authorization has been approved.
* `authorization_method` - How the card details were provided. Possible values: `chip`, `contactless`, `keyed_in`, `online`, `swipe`.
* `balance_transactions` - List of balance transactions associated with this authorization. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions) below.
* `card` - You can [create physical or virtual cards](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing) that are issued to cardholders. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card) below.
* `card_presence` - Whether the card was present at the point of sale for the authorization. Possible values: `not_present`, `present`.
* `cardholder` - The cardholder to whom this authorization belongs.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - The currency of the cardholder. This currency can be different from the currency presented at authorization and the `merchant_currency` field on this authorization. Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `fleet` - Fleet-specific information for authorizations using Fleet cards. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet) below.
* `fraud_challenges` - Fraud challenges sent to the cardholder, if this authorization was declined for fraud risk reasons. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fraud_challenges`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fraud_challenges) below.
* `fuel` - Information about fuel that was purchased with this transaction. Typically this information is received from the merchant after the authorization has been approved and the fuel dispensed. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fuel) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `merchant_amount` - The total amount that was authorized or rejected. This amount is in the `merchant_currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies#zero-decimal). `merchant_amount` should be the same as `amount`, unless `merchant_currency` and `currency` are different.
* `merchant_currency` - The local currency that was presented to the cardholder for the authorization. This currency can be different from the cardholder currency and the `currency` field on this authorization. Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `merchant_data` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.merchant_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.merchant_data) below.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `network_data` - Details about the authorization, such as identifiers, set by the card network. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.network_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.network_data) below.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `issuing.authorization`.
* `pending_request` - The pending authorization request. This field will only be non-null during an `issuing_authorization.request` webhook. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request) below.
* `request_history` - History of every time a `pending_request` authorization was approved/declined, either by you directly or by Stripe (e.g. based on your spending_controls). If the merchant changes the authorization by performing an incremental authorization, you can look at this field to see the previous requests for the authorization. This field can be helpful in determining why a given authorization was approved/declined. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history) below.
* `status` - The current status of the authorization in its lifecycle. Possible values: `closed`, `expired`, `pending`, `reversed`.
* `token` - [Token](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/tokens/object) object used for this authorization. If a network token was not used for this authorization, this field will be null.
* `transactions` - List of [transactions](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/transactions) associated with this authorization. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions) below.
* `treasury` - [Treasury](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury) details related to this authorization if it was created on a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/financial_accounts). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.treasury`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.treasury) below.
* `verification_data` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data) below.
* `verified_by_fraud_challenge` - Whether the authorization bypassed fraud risk checks because the cardholder has previously completed a fraud challenge on a similar high-risk authorization from the same merchant.
* `wallet` - The digital wallet used for this transaction. One of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, or `samsung_pay`. Will populate as `null` when no digital wallet was utilized.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.amount_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.amount_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.amount_details` attribute supports:

* `atm_fee` - The fee charged by the ATM for the cash withdrawal.
* `cashback_amount` - The amount of cash requested by the cardholder.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Gross amount of this transaction (in cents (or local equivalent)). A positive value represents funds charged to another party, and a negative value represents funds sent to another party.
* `available_on` - The date that the transaction's net funds become available in the Stripe balance.
* `balance_type` - The balance that this transaction impacts. Possible values: `issuing`, `payments`, `refund_and_dispute_prefunding`, `risk_reserved`.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `exchange_rate` - If applicable, this transaction uses an exchange rate. If money converts from currency A to currency B, then the `amount` in currency A, multiplied by the `exchange_rate`, equals the `amount` in currency B. For example, if you charge a customer 10.00 EUR, the PaymentIntent's `amount` is `1000` and `currency` is `eur`. If this converts to 12.34 USD in your Stripe account, the BalanceTransaction's `amount` is `1234`, its `currency` is `usd`, and the `exchange_rate` is `1.234`.
* `fee` - Fees (in cents (or local equivalent)) paid for this transaction. Represented as a positive integer when assessed.
* `fee_details` - Detailed breakdown of fees (in cents (or local equivalent)) paid for this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions.fee_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions.fee_details) below.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `net` - Net impact to a Stripe balance (in cents (or local equivalent)). A positive value represents incrementing a Stripe balance, and a negative value decrementing a Stripe balance. You can calculate the net impact of a transaction on a balance by `amount` - `fee`
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `balance_transaction`.
* `reporting_category` - Learn more about how [reporting categories](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/reporting-categories) can help you understand balance transactions from an accounting perspective.
* `source` - This transaction relates to the Stripe object.
* `status` - The transaction's net funds status in the Stripe balance, which are either `available` or `pending`.
* `type` - Transaction type: `tax_fund`, `adjustment`, `advance`, `advance_funding`, `anticipation_repayment`, `application_fee`, `application_fee_refund`, `charge`, `climate_order_purchase`, `climate_order_refund`, `connect_collection_transfer`, `contribution`, `inbound_transfer`, `inbound_transfer_reversal`, `issuing_authorization_hold`, `issuing_authorization_release`, `issuing_dispute`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit_reversal`, `issuing_transaction`, `obligation_outbound`, `obligation_reversal_inbound`, `payment`, `payment_failure_refund`, `payment_network_reserve_hold`, `payment_network_reserve_release`, `payment_refund`, `payment_reversal`, `payment_unreconciled`, `payout`, `payout_cancel`, `payout_failure`, `payout_minimum_balance_hold`, `payout_minimum_balance_release`, `refund`, `refund_failure`, `reserve_transaction`, `reserved_funds`, `reserve_hold`, `reserve_release`, `stripe_fee`, `stripe_fx_fee`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit_reversal`, `tax_fee`, `topup`, `topup_reversal`, `transfer`, `transfer_cancel`, `transfer_failure`, `transfer_refund`, or `fee_credit_funding`. Learn more about [balance transaction types and what they represent](https://stripe.com/docs/reports/balance-transaction-types). To classify transactions for accounting purposes, consider `reporting_category` instead. Possible values: `adjustment`, `advance`, `advance_funding`, `anticipation_repayment`, `application_fee`, `application_fee_refund`, `charge`, `climate_order_purchase`, `climate_order_refund`, `connect_collection_transfer`, `contribution`, `fee_credit_funding`, `inbound_transfer`, `inbound_transfer_reversal`, `issuing_authorization_hold`, `issuing_authorization_release`, `issuing_dispute`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit`, `issuing_dispute_provisional_credit_reversal`, `issuing_transaction`, `obligation_outbound`, `obligation_reversal_inbound`, `payment`, `payment_failure_refund`, `payment_network_reserve_hold`, `payment_network_reserve_release`, `payment_refund`, `payment_reversal`, `payment_unreconciled`, `payout`, `payout_cancel`, `payout_failure`, `payout_minimum_balance_hold`, `payout_minimum_balance_release`, `refund`, `refund_failure`, `reserve_hold`, `reserve_release`, `reserve_transaction`, `reserved_funds`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit`, `stripe_balance_payment_debit_reversal`, `stripe_fee`, `stripe_fx_fee`, `tax_fee`, `tax_fund`, `topup`, `topup_reversal`, `transfer`, `transfer_cancel`, `transfer_failure`, `transfer_refund`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions.fee_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions.fee_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.balance_transactions.fee_details` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Amount of the fee, in cents.
* `application` - ID of the Connect application that earned the fee.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `type` - Type of the fee, one of: `application_fee`, `payment_method_passthrough_fee`, `stripe_fee`, `tax`, or `withheld_tax`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card` attribute supports:

* `brand` - The brand of the card.
* `cancellation_reason` - The reason why the card was canceled. Possible values: `design_rejected`, `fulfillment_error`, `lost`, `stolen`.
* `cardholder` - An Issuing `Cardholder` object represents an individual or business entity who is [issued](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing) cards. Related guide: [How to create a cardholder](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/cards/virtual/issue-cards#create-cardholder) See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Supported currencies are `usd` in the US, `eur` in the EU, and `gbp` in the UK.
* `cvc` - The card's CVC. For security reasons, this is only available for virtual cards, and will be omitted unless you explicitly request it with [the `expand` parameter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/expanding_objects). Additionally, it's only available via the ["Retrieve a card" endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/cards/retrieve), not via "List all cards" or any other endpoint.
* `exp_month` - The expiration month of the card.
* `exp_year` - The expiration year of the card.
* `financial_account` - The financial account this card is attached to.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `last4` - The last 4 digits of the card number.
* `latest_fraud_warning` - Stripe’s assessment of whether this card’s details have been compromised. If this property isn't null, cancel and reissue the card to prevent fraudulent activity risk. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.latest_fraud_warning`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.latest_fraud_warning) below.
* `lifecycle_controls` - Rules that control the lifecycle of this card, such as automatic cancellation. Refer to our [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/controls/lifecycle-controls) for more details. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `number` - The full unredacted card number. For security reasons, this is only available for virtual cards, and will be omitted unless you explicitly request it with [the `expand` parameter](https://docs.stripe.com/api/expanding_objects). Additionally, it's only available via the ["Retrieve a card" endpoint](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/cards/retrieve), not via "List all cards" or any other endpoint.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `issuing.card`.
* `personalization_design` - The personalization design object belonging to this card.
* `replaced_by` - The latest card that replaces this card, if any.
* `replacement_for` - The card this card replaces, if any.
* `replacement_reason` - The reason why the previous card needed to be replaced. Possible values: `damaged`, `expired`, `fulfillment_error`, `lost`, `stolen`.
* `second_line` - Text separate from cardholder name, printed on the card.
* `shipping` - Where and how the card will be shipped. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping) below.
* `spending_controls` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls) below.
* `status` - Whether authorizations can be approved on this card. May be blocked from activating cards depending on past-due Cardholder requirements. Defaults to `inactive`. Possible values: `active`, `canceled`, `inactive`.
* `type` - The type of the card. Possible values: `physical`, `virtual`.
* `wallets` - Information relating to digital wallets (like Apple Pay and Google Pay). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder` attribute supports:

* `billing` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing) below.
* `company` - Additional information about a `company` cardholder. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.company`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.company) below.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `email` - The cardholder's email address.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `individual` - Additional information about an `individual` cardholder. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `name` - The cardholder's name. This will be printed on cards issued to them.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `issuing.cardholder`.
* `phone_number` - The cardholder's phone number. This is required for all cardholders who will be creating EU cards. See the [3D Secure documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/3d-secure#when-is-3d-secure-applied) for more details.
* `preferred_locales` - The cardholder’s preferred locales (languages), ordered by preference. Locales can be `de`, `en`, `es`, `fr`, or `it`. This changes the language of the [3D Secure flow](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/3d-secure) and one-time password messages sent to the cardholder.
* `requirements` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.requirements`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.requirements) below.
* `spending_controls` - Rules that control spending across this cardholder's cards. Refer to our [documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/controls/spending-controls) for more details. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls) below.
* `status` - Specifies whether to permit authorizations on this cardholder's cards. Possible values: `active`, `blocked`, `inactive`.
* `type` - One of `individual` or `company`. See [Choose a cardholder type](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/other/choose-cardholder) for more details. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing.address`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing.address) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing.address"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing.address`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.billing.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.company"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.company`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.company` attribute supports:

* `tax_id_provided` - Whether the company's business ID number was provided.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual` attribute supports:

* `card_issuing` - Information related to the card_issuing program for this cardholder. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing) below.
* `dob` - The date of birth of this cardholder. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.dob`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.dob) below.
* `first_name` - The first name of this cardholder. Required before activating Cards. This field cannot contain any numbers, special characters (except periods, commas, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes) or non-latin letters.
* `last_name` - The last name of this cardholder. Required before activating Cards. This field cannot contain any numbers, special characters (except periods, commas, hyphens, spaces and apostrophes) or non-latin letters.
* `verification` - Government-issued ID document for this cardholder. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing` attribute supports:

* `user_terms_acceptance` - Information about cardholder acceptance of Celtic [Authorized User Terms](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/compliance-us#issuing-terms). Required for cards backed by a Celtic program. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.card_issuing.user_terms_acceptance` attribute supports:

* `date` - The Unix timestamp marking when the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.
* `ip` - The IP address from which the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.
* `user_agent` - The user agent of the browser from which the cardholder accepted the Authorized User Terms.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.dob"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.dob`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.dob` attribute supports:

* `day` - The day of birth, between 1 and 31.
* `month` - The month of birth, between 1 and 12.
* `year` - The four-digit year of birth.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification` attribute supports:

* `document` - An identifying document, either a passport or local ID card. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification.document`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification.document) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification.document"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification.document`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.individual.verification.document` attribute supports:

* `back` - The back of a document returned by a [file upload](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_file) with a `purpose` value of `identity_document`.
* `front` - The front of a document returned by a [file upload](https://docs.stripe.com/api#create_file) with a `purpose` value of `identity_document`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.requirements"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.requirements`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.requirements` attribute supports:

* `disabled_reason` - If `disabled_reason` is present, all cards will decline authorizations with `cardholder_verification_required` reason. Possible values: `listed`, `rejected.listed`, `requirements.past_due`, `under_review`.
* `past_due` - Array of fields that need to be collected in order to verify and re-enable the cardholder.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls` attribute supports:

* `allowed_card_presences` - Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be allowed. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. All other statuses will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `allowed_categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to allow. All other categories will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_categories`.
* `allowed_merchant_countries` - Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be allowed. Authorizations from merchants in all other countries will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `blocked_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_card_presences` - Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be declined. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. Cannot be set with `allowed_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to decline. All other categories will be allowed. Cannot be set with `allowed_categories`.
* `blocked_merchant_countries` - Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `allowed_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `spending_limits` - Limit spending with amount-based rules that apply across this cardholder's cards. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls.spending_limits`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls.spending_limits) below.
* `spending_limits_currency` - Currency of the amounts within `spending_limits`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls.spending_limits"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls.spending_limits`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.cardholder.spending_controls.spending_limits` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Maximum amount allowed to spend per interval. This amount is in the card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) this limit applies to. Omitting this field will apply the limit to all categories.
* `interval` - Interval (or event) to which the amount applies. Possible values: `all_time`, `daily`, `monthly`, `per_authorization`, `weekly`, `yearly`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.latest_fraud_warning"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.latest_fraud_warning`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.latest_fraud_warning` attribute supports:

* `started_at` - Timestamp of the most recent fraud warning.
* `type` - The type of fraud warning that most recently took place on this card. This field updates with every new fraud warning, so the value changes over time. If populated, cancel and reissue the card. Possible values: `card_testing_exposure`, `fraud_dispute_filed`, `third_party_reported`, `user_indicated_fraud`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls` attribute supports:

* `cancel_after` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls.cancel_after`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls.cancel_after) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls.cancel_after"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls.cancel_after`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.lifecycle_controls.cancel_after` attribute supports:

* `payment_count` - The card is automatically cancelled when it makes this number of non-zero payment authorizations and transactions. The count includes penny authorizations, but doesn't include non-payment actions, such as authorization advice.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address) below.
* `address_validation` - Address validation details for the shipment. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation) below.
* `business_name` - The name of the business at the shipping address, used on the shipping label to ensure delivery when the card is shipped to a cardholder's workplace.
* `carrier` - The delivery company that shipped a card. Possible values: `correos`, `dhl`, `fedex`, `royal_mail`, `usps`.
* `customs` - Additional information that may be required for clearing customs. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.customs`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.customs) below.
* `eta` - A unix timestamp representing a best estimate of when the card will be delivered.
* `name` - Recipient name.
* `phone_number` - The phone number of the receiver of the shipment. Our courier partners will use this number to contact you in the event of card delivery issues. For individual shipments to the EU/UK, if this field is empty, we will provide them with the phone number provided when the cardholder was initially created.
* `require_signature` - Whether a signature is required for card delivery. This feature is only supported for US users. Standard shipping service does not support signature on delivery. The default value for standard shipping service is false and for express and priority services is true.
* `service` - Shipment service, such as `standard` or `express`. Possible values: `express`, `priority`, `standard`.
* `status` - The delivery status of the card. Possible values: `canceled`, `delivered`, `failure`, `pending`, `returned`, `shipped`, `submitted`.
* `tracking_number` - A tracking number for a card shipment.
* `tracking_url` - A link to the shipping carrier's site where you can view detailed information about a card shipment.
* `type` - Packaging options. Possible values: `bulk`, `individual`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation` attribute supports:

* `mode` - The address validation capabilities to use. Possible values: `disabled`, `normalization_only`, `validation_and_normalization`.
* `normalized_address` - The normalized shipping address. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation.normalized_address`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation.normalized_address) below.
* `result` - The validation result for the shipping address. Possible values: `indeterminate`, `likely_deliverable`, `likely_undeliverable`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation.normalized_address"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation.normalized_address`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.address_validation.normalized_address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.customs"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.customs`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.shipping.customs` attribute supports:

* `eori_number` - A registration number used for customs in Europe. See [https://www.gov.uk/eori](https://www.gov.uk/eori) for the UK and [https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/business/customs-procedures-import-and-export/customs-procedures/economic-operators-registration-and-identification-number-eori_en](https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/business/customs-procedures-import-and-export/customs-procedures/economic-operators-registration-and-identification-number-eori_en) for the EU.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls` attribute supports:

* `allowed_card_presences` - Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be allowed. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. All other statuses will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `allowed_categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to allow. All other categories will be blocked. Cannot be set with `blocked_categories`.
* `allowed_merchant_countries` - Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be allowed. Authorizations from merchants in all other countries will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `blocked_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_card_presences` - Array of card presence statuses from which authorizations will be declined. Possible options are `present`, `not_present`. Cannot be set with `allowed_card_presences`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `blocked_categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) of authorizations to decline. All other categories will be allowed. Cannot be set with `allowed_categories`.
* `blocked_merchant_countries` - Array of strings containing representing countries from which authorizations will be declined. Country codes should be ISO 3166 alpha-2 country codes (e.g. `US`). Cannot be set with `allowed_merchant_countries`. Provide an empty value to unset this control.
* `spending_limits` - Limit spending with amount-based rules that apply across any cards this card replaced (i.e., its `replacement_for` card and _that_ card's `replacement_for` card, up the chain). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls.spending_limits`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls.spending_limits) below.
* `spending_limits_currency` - Currency of the amounts within `spending_limits`. Always the same as the currency of the card.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls.spending_limits"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls.spending_limits`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.spending_controls.spending_limits` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - Maximum amount allowed to spend per interval. This amount is in the card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `categories` - Array of strings containing [categories](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-merchant_data-category) this limit applies to. Omitting this field will apply the limit to all categories.
* `interval` - Interval (or event) to which the amount applies. Possible values: `all_time`, `daily`, `monthly`, `per_authorization`, `weekly`, `yearly`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets` attribute supports:

* `apple_pay` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.apple_pay`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.apple_pay) below.
* `google_pay` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.google_pay`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.google_pay) below.
* `primary_account_identifier` - Unique identifier for a card used with digital wallets

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.apple_pay"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.apple_pay`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.apple_pay` attribute supports:

* `eligible` - Apple Pay Eligibility
* `ineligible_reason` - Reason the card is ineligible for Apple Pay Possible values: `missing_agreement`, `missing_cardholder_contact`, `unsupported_region`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.google_pay"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.google_pay`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.card.wallets.google_pay` attribute supports:

* `eligible` - Google Pay Eligibility
* `ineligible_reason` - Reason the card is ineligible for Google Pay Possible values: `missing_agreement`, `missing_cardholder_contact`, `unsupported_region`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet` attribute supports:

* `cardholder_prompt_data` - Answers to prompts presented to the cardholder at the point of sale. Prompted fields vary depending on the configuration of your physical fleet cards. Typical points of sale support only numeric entry. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data) below.
* `purchase_type` - The type of purchase. Possible values: `fuel_and_non_fuel_purchase`, `fuel_purchase`, `non_fuel_purchase`.
* `reported_breakdown` - More information about the total amount. Typically this information is received from the merchant after the authorization has been approved and the fuel dispensed. This information is not guaranteed to be accurate as some merchants may provide unreliable data. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown) below.
* `service_type` - The type of fuel service. Possible values: `full_service`, `non_fuel_transaction`, `self_service`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data` attribute supports:

* `alphanumeric_id` - [Deprecated] An alphanumeric ID, though typical point of sales only support numeric entry. The card program can be configured to prompt for a vehicle ID, driver ID, or generic ID.
* `driver_id` - Driver ID.
* `odometer` - Odometer reading.
* `unspecified_id` - An alphanumeric ID. This field is used when a vehicle ID, driver ID, or generic ID is entered by the cardholder, but the merchant or card network did not specify the prompt type.
* `user_id` - User ID.
* `vehicle_number` - Vehicle number.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown` attribute supports:

* `fuel` - Breakdown of fuel portion of the purchase. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel) below.
* `non_fuel` - Breakdown of non-fuel portion of the purchase. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel) below.
* `tax` - Information about tax included in this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross fuel amount that should equal Fuel Quantity multiplied by Fuel Unit Cost, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross non-fuel amount that should equal the sum of the line items, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax` attribute supports:

* `local_amount_decimal` - Amount of state or provincial Sales Tax included in the transaction amount. `null` if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.
* `national_amount_decimal` - Amount of national Sales Tax or VAT included in the transaction amount. `null` if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fraud_challenges"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fraud_challenges`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fraud_challenges` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `channel` - The method by which the fraud challenge was delivered to the cardholder. Possible values: `sms`.
* `status` - The status of the fraud challenge. Possible values: `expired`, `pending`, `rejected`, `undeliverable`, `verified`.
* `undeliverable_reason` - If the challenge is not deliverable, the reason why. Possible values: `no_phone_number`, `unsupported_phone_number`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.fuel"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.fuel` attribute supports:

* `industry_product_code` - [Conexxus Payment System Product Code](https://www.conexxus.org/conexxus-payment-system-product-codes) identifying the primary fuel product purchased.
* `quantity_decimal` - The quantity of `unit`s of fuel that was dispensed, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.
* `type` - The type of fuel that was purchased. Possible values: `diesel`, `other`, `unleaded_plus`, `unleaded_regular`, `unleaded_super`.
* `unit` - The units for `quantity_decimal`. Possible values: `charging_minute`, `imperial_gallon`, `kilogram`, `kilowatt_hour`, `liter`, `other`, `pound`, `us_gallon`.
* `unit_cost_decimal` - The cost in cents per each unit of fuel, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.merchant_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.merchant_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.merchant_data` attribute supports:

* `category` - A categorization of the seller's type of business. See our [merchant categories guide](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/merchant-categories) for a list of possible values.
* `category_code` - The merchant category code for the seller’s business
* `city` - City where the seller is located
* `country` - Country where the seller is located
* `name` - Name of the seller
* `network_id` - Identifier assigned to the seller by the card network. Different card networks may assign different network_id fields to the same merchant.
* `postal_code` - Postal code where the seller is located
* `state` - State where the seller is located
* `tax_id` - The seller's tax identification number. Currently populated for French merchants only.
* `terminal_id` - An ID assigned by the seller to the location of the sale.
* `url` - URL provided by the merchant on a 3DS request

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.network_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.network_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.network_data` attribute supports:

* `acquiring_institution_id` - Identifier assigned to the acquirer by the card network. Sometimes this value is not provided by the network; in this case, the value will be `null`.
* `system_trace_audit_number` - The System Trace Audit Number (STAN) is a 6-digit identifier assigned by the acquirer. Prefer `network_data.transaction_id` if present, unless you have special requirements.
* `transaction_id` - Unique identifier for the authorization assigned by the card network used to match subsequent messages, disputes, and transactions.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The additional amount Stripe will hold if the authorization is approved, in the card's [currency](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorization_object-pending-request-currency) and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `amount_details` - Detailed breakdown of amount components. These amounts are denominated in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request.amount_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request.amount_details) below.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `is_amount_controllable` - If set `true`, you may provide [amount](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/authorizations/approve#approve_issuing_authorization-amount) to control how much to hold for the authorization.
* `merchant_amount` - The amount the merchant is requesting to be authorized in the `merchant_currency`. The amount is in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `merchant_currency` - The local currency the merchant is requesting to authorize.
* `network_risk_score` - The card network's estimate of the likelihood that an authorization is fraudulent. Takes on values between 1 and 99.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request.amount_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request.amount_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.pending_request.amount_details` attribute supports:

* `atm_fee` - The fee charged by the ATM for the cash withdrawal.
* `cashback_amount` - The amount of cash requested by the cardholder.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The `pending_request.amount` at the time of the request, presented in your card's currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). Stripe held this amount from your account to fund the authorization if the request was approved.
* `amount_details` - Detailed breakdown of amount components. These amounts are denominated in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history.amount_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history.amount_details) below.
* `approved` - Whether this request was approved.
* `authorization_code` - A code created by Stripe which is shared with the merchant to validate the authorization. This field will be populated if the authorization message was approved. The code typically starts with the letter "S", followed by a six-digit number. For example, "S498162". Please note that the code is not guaranteed to be unique across authorizations.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `merchant_amount` - The `pending_request.merchant_amount` at the time of the request, presented in the `merchant_currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `merchant_currency` - The currency that was collected by the merchant and presented to the cardholder for the authorization. Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `network_risk_score` - The card network's estimate of the likelihood that an authorization is fraudulent. Takes on values between 1 and 99.
* `reason` - When an authorization is approved or declined by you or by Stripe, this field provides additional detail on the reason for the outcome. Possible values: `account_disabled`, `card_active`, `card_canceled`, `card_expired`, `card_inactive`, `cardholder_blocked`, `cardholder_inactive`, `cardholder_verification_required`, `insecure_authorization_method`, `insufficient_funds`, `network_fallback`, `not_allowed`, `pin_blocked`, `spending_controls`, `stripe_internal_error`, `suspected_fraud`, `verification_failed`, `webhook_approved`, `webhook_declined`, `webhook_error`, `webhook_timeout`.
* `reason_message` - If the `request_history.reason` is `webhook_error` because the direct webhook response is invalid (for example, parsing errors or missing parameters), we surface a more detailed error message via this field.
* `requested_at` - Time when the card network received an authorization request from the acquirer in UTC. Referred to by networks as transmission time.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history.amount_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history.amount_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.request_history.amount_details` attribute supports:

* `atm_fee` - The fee charged by the ATM for the cash withdrawal.
* `cashback_amount` - The amount of cash requested by the cardholder.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `amount` - The transaction amount, which will be reflected in your balance. This amount is in your currency and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal).
* `amount_details` - Detailed breakdown of amount components. These amounts are denominated in `currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.amount_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.amount_details) below.
* `authorization` - The `Authorization` object that led to this transaction.
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the [balance transaction](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance_transactions) associated with this transaction.
* `card` - The card used to make this transaction.
* `cardholder` - The cardholder to whom this transaction belongs.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `dispute` - If you've disputed the transaction, the ID of the dispute.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `merchant_amount` - The amount that the merchant will receive, denominated in `merchant_currency` and in the [smallest currency unit](https://docs.stripe.com/currencies#zero-decimal). It will be different from `amount` if the merchant is taking payment in a different currency.
* `merchant_currency` - The currency with which the merchant is taking payment.
* `merchant_data` - See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.merchant_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.merchant_data) below.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `network_data` - Details about the transaction, such as processing dates, set by the card network. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.network_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.network_data) below.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `issuing.transaction`.
* `purchase_details` - Additional purchase information that is optionally provided by the merchant. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details) below.
* `token` - [Token](https://docs.stripe.com/api/issuing/tokens/object) object used for this transaction. If a network token was not used for this transaction, this field will be null.
* `treasury` - [Treasury](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury) details related to this transaction if it was created on a [FinancialAccount](/docs/api/treasury/financial_accounts See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.treasury`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.treasury) below.
* `type` - The nature of the transaction. Possible values: `capture`, `refund`.
* `wallet` - The digital wallet used for this transaction. One of `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, or `samsung_pay`. Possible values: `apple_pay`, `google_pay`, `samsung_pay`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.amount_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.amount_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.amount_details` attribute supports:

* `atm_fee` - The fee charged by the ATM for the cash withdrawal.
* `cashback_amount` - The amount of cash requested by the cardholder.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.merchant_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.merchant_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.merchant_data` attribute supports:

* `category` - A categorization of the seller's type of business. See our [merchant categories guide](https://docs.stripe.com/issuing/merchant-categories) for a list of possible values.
* `category_code` - The merchant category code for the seller’s business
* `city` - City where the seller is located
* `country` - Country where the seller is located
* `name` - Name of the seller
* `network_id` - Identifier assigned to the seller by the card network. Different card networks may assign different network_id fields to the same merchant.
* `postal_code` - Postal code where the seller is located
* `state` - State where the seller is located
* `tax_id` - The seller's tax identification number. Currently populated for French merchants only.
* `terminal_id` - An ID assigned by the seller to the location of the sale.
* `url` - URL provided by the merchant on a 3DS request

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.network_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.network_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.network_data` attribute supports:

* `authorization_code` - A code created by Stripe which is shared with the merchant to validate the authorization. This field will be populated if the authorization message was approved. The code typically starts with the letter "S", followed by a six-digit number. For example, "S498162". Please note that the code is not guaranteed to be unique across authorizations.
* `processing_date` - The date the transaction was processed by the card network. This can be different from the date the seller recorded the transaction depending on when the acquirer submits the transaction to the network.
* `transaction_id` - Unique identifier for the authorization assigned by the card network used to match subsequent messages, disputes, and transactions.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details` attribute supports:

* `fleet` - Fleet-specific information for transactions using Fleet cards. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet) below.
* `flight` - Information about the flight that was purchased with this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight) below.
* `fuel` - Information about fuel that was purchased with this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fuel) below.
* `lodging` - Information about lodging that was purchased with this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.lodging`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.lodging) below.
* `receipt` - The line items in the purchase. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.receipt`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.receipt) below.
* `reference` - A merchant-specific order number.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet` attribute supports:

* `cardholder_prompt_data` - Answers to prompts presented to cardholder at point of sale. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data) below.
* `purchase_type` - The type of purchase. One of `fuel_purchase`, `non_fuel_purchase`, or `fuel_and_non_fuel_purchase`.
* `reported_breakdown` - More information about the total amount. This information is not guaranteed to be accurate as some merchants may provide unreliable data. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown) below.
* `service_type` - The type of fuel service. One of `non_fuel_transaction`, `full_service`, or `self_service`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.cardholder_prompt_data` attribute supports:

* `driver_id` - Driver ID.
* `odometer` - Odometer reading.
* `unspecified_id` - An alphanumeric ID. This field is used when a vehicle ID, driver ID, or generic ID is entered by the cardholder, but the merchant or card network did not specify the prompt type.
* `user_id` - User ID.
* `vehicle_number` - Vehicle number.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown` attribute supports:

* `fuel` - Breakdown of fuel portion of the purchase. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel) below.
* `non_fuel` - Breakdown of non-fuel portion of the purchase. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel) below.
* `tax` - Information about tax included in this transaction. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel"></a>
