### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross fuel amount that should equal Fuel Volume multiplied by Fuel Unit Cost, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.non_fuel` attribute supports:

* `gross_amount_decimal` - Gross non-fuel amount that should equal the sum of the line items, inclusive of taxes.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fleet.reported_breakdown.tax` attribute supports:

* `local_amount_decimal` - Amount of state or provincial Sales Tax included in the transaction amount. Null if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.
* `national_amount_decimal` - Amount of national Sales Tax or VAT included in the transaction amount. Null if not reported by merchant or not subject to tax.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight` attribute supports:

* `departure_at` - The time that the flight departed.
* `passenger_name` - The name of the passenger.
* `refundable` - Whether the ticket is refundable.
* `segments` - The legs of the trip. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight.segments`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight.segments) below.
* `travel_agency` - The travel agency that issued the ticket.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight.segments"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight.segments`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.flight.segments` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `arrival_airport_code` - The three-letter IATA airport code of the flight's destination.
* `carrier` - The airline carrier code.
* `departure_airport_code` - The three-letter IATA airport code that the flight departed from.
* `flight_number` - The flight number.
* `service_class` - The flight's service class.
* `stopover_allowed` - Whether a stopover is allowed on this flight.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fuel"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fuel`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.fuel` attribute supports:

* `industry_product_code` - [Conexxus Payment System Product Code](https://www.conexxus.org/conexxus-payment-system-product-codes) identifying the primary fuel product purchased.
* `quantity_decimal` - The quantity of `unit`s of fuel that was dispensed, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.
* `type` - The type of fuel that was purchased. One of `diesel`, `unleaded_plus`, `unleaded_regular`, `unleaded_super`, or `other`.
* `unit` - The units for `quantity_decimal`. One of `charging_minute`, `imperial_gallon`, `kilogram`, `kilowatt_hour`, `liter`, `pound`, `us_gallon`, or `other`.
* `unit_cost_decimal` - The cost in cents per each unit of fuel, represented as a decimal string with at most 12 decimal places.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.lodging"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.lodging`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.lodging` attribute supports:

* `check_in_at` - The time of checking into the lodging.
* `nights` - The number of nights stayed at the lodging.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.receipt"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.receipt`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.purchase_details.receipt` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `description` - The description of the item. The maximum length of this field is 26 characters.
* `quantity` - The quantity of the item.
* `total` - The total for this line item in cents.
* `unit_cost` - The unit cost of the item in cents.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.treasury"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.treasury`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.transactions.treasury` attribute supports:

* `received_credit` - The Treasury [ReceivedCredit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_credits) representing this Issuing transaction if it is a refund
* `received_debit` - The Treasury [ReceivedDebit](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_debits) representing this Issuing transaction if it is a capture

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.treasury"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.treasury`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.treasury` attribute supports:

* `received_credits` - The array of [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_credits) associated with this authorization
* `received_debits` - The array of [ReceivedDebits](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/received_debits) associated with this authorization
* `transaction` - The Treasury [Transaction](https://docs.stripe.com/api/treasury/transactions) associated with this authorization

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data` attribute supports:

* `address_line1_check` - Whether the cardholder provided an address first line and if it matched the cardholder’s `billing.address.line1`. Possible values: `match`, `mismatch`, `not_provided`.
* `address_postal_code_check` - Whether the cardholder provided a postal code and if it matched the cardholder’s `billing.address.postal_code`. Possible values: `match`, `mismatch`, `not_provided`.
* `authentication_exemption` - The exemption applied to this authorization. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.authentication_exemption`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.authentication_exemption) below.
* `cvc_check` - Whether the cardholder provided a CVC and if it matched Stripe’s record. Possible values: `match`, `mismatch`, `not_provided`.
* `expiry_check` - Whether the cardholder provided an expiry date and if it matched Stripe’s record. Possible values: `match`, `mismatch`, `not_provided`.
* `postal_code` - The postal code submitted as part of the authorization used for postal code verification.
* `three_d_secure` - 3D Secure details. See [`flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.three_d_secure`](#flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.three_d_secure) below.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.authentication_exemption"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.authentication_exemption`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.authentication_exemption` attribute supports:

* `claimed_by` - The entity that requested the exemption, either the acquiring merchant or the Issuing user. Possible values: `acquirer`, `issuer`.
* `type` - The specific exemption claimed for this authorization. Possible values: `low_value_transaction`, `transaction_risk_analysis`, `unknown`.

<a id="flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.three_d_secure"></a>
### `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.three_d_secure`

The `flow_details.issuing_authorization.verification_data.three_d_secure` attribute supports:

* `result` - The outcome of the 3D Secure authentication request. Possible values: `attempt_acknowledged`, `authenticated`, `failed`, `required`.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - ID of the [customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers) to whom an OutboundPayment is sent.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination_payment_method` - The PaymentMethod via which an OutboundPayment is sent. This field can be empty if the OutboundPayment was created using `destination_payment_method_data`.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - Details about the PaymentMethod for an OutboundPayment. See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `end_user_details` - Details about the end user. See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.outbound_payment`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundPayment. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - The description that appears on the receiving end for an OutboundPayment (for example, bank statement for external bank transfer).
* `status` - Current status of the OutboundPayment: `processing`, `failed`, `posted`, `returned`, `canceled`. An OutboundPayment is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundPayment has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundPayment fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `posted`, `processing`, `returned`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the OutboundPayment. Possible values: `financial_account`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - Token of the FinancialAccount.
* `network` - The rails used to send funds. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details` attribute supports:

* `ip_address` - IP address of the user initiating the OutboundPayment. Set if `present` is set to `true`. IP address collection is required for risk and compliance reasons. This will be used to help determine if the OutboundPayment is authorized or should be blocked.
* `present` - `true` if the OutboundPayment creation request is being made on behalf of an end user by a platform. Otherwise, `false`.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the return. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `declined`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `canceled`.
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `failed`.
* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `posted`.
* `returned_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `returned`.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details` attribute supports:

* `ach` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach) below.
* `type` - The US bank account network used to send funds. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `us_domestic_wire` - See [`flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`](#flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire) below.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach` attribute supports:

* `trace_id` - ACH trace ID of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `ach` network.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`

The `flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire` attribute supports:

* `chips` - CHIPS System Sequence Number (SSN) of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `imad` - IMAD of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `omad` - OMAD of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.

<a id="flow_details.outbound_transfer"></a>
### `flow_details.outbound_transfer`

The `flow_details.outbound_transfer` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination_payment_method` - The PaymentMethod used as the payment instrument for an OutboundTransfer.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.outbound_transfer`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundTransfer. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - Information about the OutboundTransfer to be sent to the recipient account.
* `status` - Current status of the OutboundTransfer: `processing`, `failed`, `canceled`, `posted`, `returned`. An OutboundTransfer is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundTransfer has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundTransfer fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `posted`, `processing`, `returned`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details`](#flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit`

The `flow_details.received_credit` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `failure_code` - Reason for the failure. A ReceivedCredit might fail because the receiving FinancialAccount is closed or frozen. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `international_transaction`, `other`.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that received the funds.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `initiating_payment_method_details` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details) below.
* `linked_flows` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `network` - The rails used to send the funds. Possible values: `ach`, `card`, `rtp`, `stripe`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.received_credit`.
* `reversal_details` - Details describing when a ReceivedCredit may be reversed. See [`flow_details.received_credit.reversal_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.reversal_details) below.
* `status` - Status of the ReceivedCredit. ReceivedCredits are created either `succeeded` (approved) or `failed` (declined). If a ReceivedCredit is declined, the failure reason can be found in the `failure_code` field. Possible values: `failed`, `succeeded`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `balance` - Set when `type` is `balance`. Possible values: `payments`.
* `billing_details` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `issuing_card` - Set when `type` is `issuing_card`. This is an [Issuing Card](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_cards) ID.
* `type` - Polymorphic type matching the originating money movement's source. This can be an external account, a Stripe balance, or a FinancialAccount. Possible values: `balance`, `financial_account`, `issuing_card`, `stripe`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - The FinancialAccount ID.
* `network` - The rails the ReceivedCredit was sent over. A FinancialAccount can only send funds over `stripe`. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Bank name.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the bank account number.
* `routing_number` - The routing number for the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows` attribute supports:

* `credit_reversal` - The CreditReversal created as a result of this ReceivedCredit being reversed.
* `issuing_authorization` - Set if the ReceivedCredit was created due to an [Issuing Authorization](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorizations) object.
* `issuing_transaction` - Set if the ReceivedCredit is also viewable as an [Issuing transaction](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_transactions) object.
* `source_flow` - ID of the source flow. Set if `network` is `stripe` and the source flow is visible to the user. Examples of source flows include OutboundPayments, payouts, or CreditReversals.
* `source_flow_details` - The expandable object of the source flow. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details) below.
* `source_flow_type` - The type of flow that originated the ReceivedCredit (for example, `outbound_payment`).

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details` attribute supports:

* `credit_reversal` - You can reverse some [ReceivedCredits](https://docs.stripe.com/api#received_credits) depending on their network and source flow. Reversing a ReceivedCredit leads to the creation of a new object known as a CreditReversal. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal) below.
* `outbound_payment` - Use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) to send funds to another party's external bank account or [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts). To send money to an account belonging to the same user, use an [OutboundTransfer](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_transfers). Simulate OutboundPayment state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_payments` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundPayment objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-payments) See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment) below.
* `outbound_transfer` - Use [OutboundTransfers](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) to transfer funds from a [FinancialAccount](https://docs.stripe.com/api#financial_accounts) to a PaymentMethod belonging to the same entity. To send funds to a different party, use [OutboundPayments](https://docs.stripe.com/api#outbound_payments) instead. You can send funds over ACH rails or through a domestic wire transfer to a user's own external bank account. Simulate OutboundTransfer state changes with the `/v1/test_helpers/treasury/outbound_transfers` endpoints. These methods can only be called on test mode objects. Related guide: [Moving money with Treasury using OutboundTransfer objects](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/treasury/moving-money/financial-accounts/out-of/outbound-transfers) See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer) below.
* `payout` - A `Payout` object is created when you receive funds from Stripe, or when you initiate a payout to either a bank account or debit card of a [connected Stripe account](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/connect/bank-debit-card-payouts). You can retrieve individual payouts, and list all payouts. Payouts are made on [varying schedules](https://docs.stripe.com/docs/connect/manage-payout-schedule), depending on your country and industry. Related guide: [Receiving payouts](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts) See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout) below.
* `type` - The type of the source flow that originated the ReceivedCredit. Possible values: `credit_reversal`, `other`, `outbound_payment`, `outbound_transfer`, `payout`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount to reverse funds from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `network` - The rails used to reverse the funds. Possible values: `ach`, `stripe`.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.credit_reversal`.
* `received_credit` - The ReceivedCredit being reversed.
* `status` - Status of the CreditReversal Possible values: `canceled`, `posted`, `processing`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.credit_reversal.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when the CreditReversal changed status to `posted`

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `customer` - ID of the [customer](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customers) to whom an OutboundPayment is sent.
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination_payment_method` - The PaymentMethod via which an OutboundPayment is sent. This field can be empty if the OutboundPayment was created using `destination_payment_method_data`.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - Details about the PaymentMethod for an OutboundPayment. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `end_user_details` - Details about the end user. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.outbound_payment`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundPayment. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - The description that appears on the receiving end for an OutboundPayment (for example, bank statement for external bank transfer).
* `status` - Current status of the OutboundPayment: `processing`, `failed`, `posted`, `returned`, `canceled`. An OutboundPayment is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundPayment has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundPayment fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `posted`, `processing`, `returned`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the OutboundPayment. Possible values: `financial_account`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - Token of the FinancialAccount.
* `network` - The rails used to send funds. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.end_user_details` attribute supports:

* `ip_address` - IP address of the user initiating the OutboundPayment. Set if `present` is set to `true`. IP address collection is required for risk and compliance reasons. This will be used to help determine if the OutboundPayment is authorized or should be blocked.
* `present` - `true` if the OutboundPayment creation request is being made on behalf of an end user by a platform. Otherwise, `false`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.returned_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the return. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `declined`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `canceled`.
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `failed`.
* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `posted`.
* `returned_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundPayment changed status to `returned`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details` attribute supports:

* `ach` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach) below.
* `type` - The US bank account network used to send funds. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `us_domestic_wire` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.ach` attribute supports:

* `trace_id` - ACH trace ID of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `ach` network.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_payment.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire` attribute supports:

* `chips` - CHIPS System Sequence Number (SSN) of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `imad` - IMAD of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `omad` - OMAD of the OutboundPayment for payments sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `cancelable` - Returns `true` if the object can be canceled, and `false` otherwise.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination_payment_method` - The PaymentMethod used as the payment instrument for an OutboundTransfer.
* `destination_payment_method_details` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details) below.
* `expected_arrival_date` - The date when funds are expected to arrive in the destination account.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.outbound_transfer`.
* `returned_details` - Details about a returned OutboundTransfer. Only set when the status is `returned`. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details) below.
* `statement_descriptor` - Information about the OutboundTransfer to be sent to the recipient account.
* `status` - Current status of the OutboundTransfer: `processing`, `failed`, `canceled`, `posted`, `returned`. An OutboundTransfer is `processing` if it has been created and is pending. The status changes to `posted` once the OutboundTransfer has been "confirmed" and funds have left the account, or to `failed` or `canceled`. If an OutboundTransfer fails to arrive at its destination, its status will change to `returned`. Possible values: `canceled`, `failed`, `posted`, `processing`, `returned`.
* `status_transitions` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions) below.
* `tracking_details` - Details about network-specific tracking information if available. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details) below.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `billing_details` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `type` - The type of the payment method used in the OutboundTransfer. Possible values: `financial_account`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - Token of the FinancialAccount.
* `network` - The rails used to send funds. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.destination_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `account_holder_type` - Account holder type: individual or company. Possible values: `company`, `individual`.
* `account_type` - Account type: checkings or savings. Defaults to checking if omitted. Possible values: `checking`, `savings`.
* `bank_name` - Name of the bank associated with the bank account.
* `fingerprint` - Uniquely identifies this particular bank account. You can use this attribute to check whether two bank accounts are the same.
* `last4` - Last four digits of the bank account number.
* `mandate` - ID of the mandate used to make this payment.
* `network` - The network rails used. See the [docs](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/money-movement/timelines) to learn more about money movement timelines for each network type. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `routing_number` - Routing number of the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.returned_details` attribute supports:

* `code` - Reason for the return. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `bank_account_restricted`, `bank_ownership_changed`, `declined`, `incorrect_account_holder_name`, `invalid_account_number`, `invalid_currency`, `no_account`, `other`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `canceled_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `canceled`
* `failed_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `failed`
* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `posted`
* `returned_at` - Timestamp describing when an OutboundTransfer changed status to `returned`

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details` attribute supports:

* `ach` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.ach`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.ach) below.
* `type` - The US bank account network used to send funds. Possible values: `ach`, `us_domestic_wire`.
* `us_domestic_wire` - See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.ach"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.ach`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.ach` attribute supports:

* `trace_id` - ACH trace ID of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `ach` network.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.outbound_transfer.tracking_details.us_domestic_wire` attribute supports:

* `chips` - CHIPS System Sequence Number (SSN) of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `imad` - IMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.
* `omad` - OMAD of the OutboundTransfer for transfers sent over the `us_domestic_wire` network.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout` attribute supports:

* `amount` - The amount (in cents (or local equivalent)) that transfers to your bank account or debit card.
* `application_fee` - The application fee (if any) for the payout. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/instant-payouts#monetization-and-fees) for details.
* `application_fee_amount` - The amount of the application fee (if any) requested for the payout. [See the Connect documentation](https://docs.stripe.com/connect/instant-payouts#monetization-and-fees) for details.
* `arrival_date` - Date that you can expect the payout to arrive in the bank. This factors in delays to account for weekends or bank holidays.
* `automatic` - Returns `true` if the payout is created by an [automated payout schedule](https://docs.stripe.com/payouts#payout-schedule) and `false` if it's [requested manually](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts#manual-payouts).
* `balance_transaction` - ID of the balance transaction that describes the impact of this payout on your account balance.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `destination` - ID of the bank account or card the payout is sent to.
* `failure_balance_transaction` - If the payout fails or cancels, this is the ID of the balance transaction that reverses the initial balance transaction and returns the funds from the failed payout back in your balance.
* `failure_code` - Error code that provides a reason for a payout failure, if available. View our [list of failure codes](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payout_failures).
* `failure_message` - Message that provides the reason for a payout failure, if available.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `metadata` - Set of [key-value pairs](https://docs.stripe.com/api/metadata) that you can attach to an object. This can be useful for storing additional information about the object in a structured format.
* `method` - The method used to send this payout, which can be `standard` or `instant`. `instant` is supported for payouts to debit cards and bank accounts in certain countries. Learn more about [bank support for Instant Payouts](https://stripe.com/docs/payouts/instant-payouts-banks).
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `payout`.
* `original_payout` - If the payout reverses another, this is the ID of the original payout.
* `payout_method` - ID of the v2 FinancialAccount the funds are sent to.
* `reconciliation_status` - If `completed`, you can use the [Balance Transactions API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/balance_transactions/list#balance_transaction_list-payout) to list all balance transactions that are paid out in this payout. Possible values: `completed`, `in_progress`, `not_applicable`.
* `reversed_by` - If the payout reverses, this is the ID of the payout that reverses this payout.
* `source_type` - The source balance this payout came from, which can be one of the following: `card`, `fpx`, or `bank_account`.
* `statement_descriptor` - Extra information about a payout that displays on the user's bank statement.
* `status` - Current status of the payout: `paid`, `pending`, `in_transit`, `canceled` or `failed`. A payout is `pending` until it's submitted to the bank, when it becomes `in_transit`. The status changes to `paid` if the transaction succeeds, or to `failed` or `canceled` (within 5 business days). Some payouts that fail might initially show as `paid`, then change to `failed`.
* `trace_id` - A value that generates from the beneficiary's bank that allows users to track payouts with their bank. Banks might call this a "reference number" or something similar. See [`flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout.trace_id`](#flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout.trace_id) below.
* `type` - Can be `bank_account` or `card`. Possible values: `bank_account`, `card`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout.trace_id"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout.trace_id`

The `flow_details.received_credit.linked_flows.source_flow_details.payout.trace_id` attribute supports:

* `status` - Possible values are `pending`, `supported`, and `unsupported`. When `payout.status` is `pending` or `in_transit`, this will be `pending`. When the payout transitions to `paid`, `failed`, or `canceled`, this status will become `supported` or `unsupported` shortly after in most cases. In some cases, this may appear as `pending` for up to 10 days after `arrival_date` until transitioning to `supported` or `unsupported`.
* `value` - The trace ID value if `trace_id.status` is `supported`, otherwise `nil`.

<a id="flow_details.received_credit.reversal_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_credit.reversal_details`

The `flow_details.received_credit.reversal_details` attribute supports:

* `deadline` - Time before which a ReceivedCredit can be reversed.
* `restricted_reason` - Set if a ReceivedCredit cannot be reversed. Possible values: `already_reversed`, `deadline_passed`, `network_restricted`, `other`, `source_flow_restricted`.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit`

The `flow_details.received_debit` attribute supports:

* `amount` - Amount (in cents) transferred.
* `created` - Time at which the object was created. Measured in seconds since the Unix epoch.
* `currency` - Three-letter [ISO currency code](https://www.iso.org/iso-4217-currency-codes.html), in lowercase. Must be a [supported currency](https://stripe.com/docs/currencies).
* `description` - An arbitrary string attached to the object. Often useful for displaying to users.
* `failure_code` - Reason for the failure. A ReceivedDebit might fail because the FinancialAccount doesn't have sufficient funds, is closed, or is frozen. Possible values: `account_closed`, `account_frozen`, `insufficient_funds`, `international_transaction`, `other`.
* `financial_account` - The FinancialAccount that funds were pulled from.
* `hosted_regulatory_receipt_url` - A [hosted transaction receipt](https://docs.stripe.com/treasury/moving-money/regulatory-receipts) URL that is provided when money movement is considered regulated under Stripe's money transmission licenses.
* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `initiating_payment_method_details` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details`](#flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details) below.
* `linked_flows` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.linked_flows`](#flow_details.received_debit.linked_flows) below.
* `livemode` - If the object exists in live mode, the value is `true`. If the object exists in test mode, the value is `false`.
* `network` - The network used for the ReceivedDebit. Possible values: `ach`, `card`, `stripe`.
* `object` - String representing the object's type. Objects of the same type share the same value. Possible values: `treasury.received_debit`.
* `reversal_details` - Details describing when a ReceivedDebit might be reversed. See [`flow_details.received_debit.reversal_details`](#flow_details.received_debit.reversal_details) below.
* `status` - Status of the ReceivedDebit. ReceivedDebits are created with a status of either `succeeded` (approved) or `failed` (declined). The failure reason can be found under the `failure_code`. Possible values: `failed`, `succeeded`.
* `transaction` - The Transaction associated with this object.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details`

The `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details` attribute supports:

* `balance` - Set when `type` is `balance`. Possible values: `payments`.
* `billing_details` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details`](#flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details) below.
* `financial_account` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account`](#flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account) below.
* `issuing_card` - Set when `type` is `issuing_card`. This is an [Issuing Card](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_cards) ID.
* `type` - Polymorphic type matching the originating money movement's source. This can be an external account, a Stripe balance, or a FinancialAccount. Possible values: `balance`, `financial_account`, `issuing_card`, `stripe`, `us_bank_account`.
* `us_bank_account` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`](#flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account) below.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details`

The `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details` attribute supports:

* `address` - See [`flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`](#flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address) below.
* `email` - Email address.
* `name` - Full name.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address`

The `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.billing_details.address` attribute supports:

* `city` - City, district, suburb, town, or village.
* `country` - Two-letter country code ([ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
* `line1` - Address line 1, such as the street, PO Box, or company name.
* `line2` - Address line 2, such as the apartment, suite, unit, or building.
* `postal_code` - ZIP or postal code.
* `state` - State, county, province, or region ([ISO 3166-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-2)).

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account`

The `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.financial_account` attribute supports:

* `id` - The FinancialAccount ID.
* `network` - The rails the ReceivedCredit was sent over. A FinancialAccount can only send funds over `stripe`. Possible values: `stripe`.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account`

The `flow_details.received_debit.initiating_payment_method_details.us_bank_account` attribute supports:

* `bank_name` - Bank name.
* `last4` - The last four digits of the bank account number.
* `routing_number` - The routing number for the bank account.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.linked_flows"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.linked_flows`

The `flow_details.received_debit.linked_flows` attribute supports:

* `debit_reversal` - The DebitReversal created as a result of this ReceivedDebit being reversed.
* `inbound_transfer` - Set if the ReceivedDebit is associated with an InboundTransfer's return of funds.
* `issuing_authorization` - Set if the ReceivedDebit was created due to an [Issuing Authorization](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_authorizations) object.
* `issuing_transaction` - Set if the ReceivedDebit is also viewable as an [Issuing Dispute](https://docs.stripe.com/api#issuing_disputes) object.
* `payout` - Set if the ReceivedDebit was created due to a [Payout](https://docs.stripe.com/api#payouts) object.
* `topup` - Set if the ReceivedDebit was created due to a [Topup](https://docs.stripe.com/api#topups) object.

<a id="flow_details.received_debit.reversal_details"></a>
### `flow_details.received_debit.reversal_details`

The `flow_details.received_debit.reversal_details` attribute supports:

* `deadline` - Time before which a ReceivedDebit can be reversed.
* `restricted_reason` - Set if a ReceivedDebit can't be reversed. Possible values: `already_reversed`, `deadline_passed`, `network_restricted`, `other`, `source_flow_restricted`.

<a id="status_transitions"></a>
### `status_transitions`

The `status_transitions` attribute supports:

* `posted_at` - Timestamp describing when the Transaction changed status to `posted`.
* `void_at` - Timestamp describing when the Transaction changed status to `void`.
